content: 1. Administer peginterferon alfa-2a subcutaneously at a dose of 73 mcg/m² body surface area (maximum dose: 180 mcg) once weekly for 48 weeks. 2. Conduct pregnancy screening for females of childbearing potential prior to initiating therapy. 3. Peginterferon alfa-2a increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Fezolinetant's area under the curve (AUC) and peak plasma concentration are elevated when co-administered with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors. 4. Peginterferon alfa-2a increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. Co-administration of peginterferon alfa-2a and deferiprone increases the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If deferiprone must be used, avoid combining it with other drugs associated with neutropenia or agranulocytosis, and monitor absolute neutrophil count more frequently. 6. Peginterferon alfa-2a increases the levels or effects of duloxetine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 7. Peginterferon alfa-2a and pexidartinib both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Avoid co-administration with other hepatotoxic agents. 8. Peginterferon alfa-2a and pretomanid increase each other's toxicity. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol, hepatotoxic agents, herbal supplements, and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid during therapy. 9. Peginterferon alfa-2a increases the levels or effects of tizanidine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 10. Peginterferon alfa-2a and ropeginterferon alfa-2b increase each other's toxicity due to additive myelosuppression. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Monitor for excessive myelosuppression if co-administered. 11. Peginterferon alfa-2a increases the levels or effects of clomipramine, clozapine, imipramine, lidocaine, mexiletine, olanzapine, rasagiline, ropinirole, theophylline, and warfarin by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Peginterferon alfa-2a increases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Peginterferon alfa-2a increases the levels or effects of minor substrates such as antipyrine, asenapine, caffeine, frovatriptan, ondansetron, and riluzole by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 14. Peginterferon alfa-2a and hydroxyurea may cause cutaneous vasculitic toxicities, such as vasculitic ulcerations and gangrene, particularly in patients with a history of interferon therapy. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Peginterferon alfa-2a and ifosfamide increase each other's toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Ifosfamide may enhance the toxicities of myelosuppressive agents. Monitor for increased risk of myelosuppression. 16. Peginterferon alfa-2a and lamivudine increase each other's toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy, leading to an increased risk of liver decompensation. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Pegloticase decreases the levels or effects of peginterferon alfa-2a due to the potential development of anti-PEG antibodies. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 18. Pegvaliase-treated patients often develop anti-polyethylene glycol (PEG) IgM and IgG antibodies. The risk of co-administration with other PEGylated products is unknown. There is a case report of anaphylaxis following a medroxyprogesterone acetate injectable suspension containing PEG 3350. Carefully review all drug labels, including over-the-counter products, for PEG content. 19. Peginterferon alfa-2a increases the effects of valoctocogene roxaparvovec, which may potentiate the risk of elevated liver enzymes when combined with hepatotoxic medications. Monitor closely and consider alternative medications. 20. Peginterferon alfa-2a may cause or exacerbate fatal or life-threatening neuropsychiatric, autoimmune, ischemic, and infectious disorders. Monitor patients closely with periodic clinical and laboratory evaluations. Discontinue therapy if severe or worsening symptoms persist, as these conditions typically resolve after stopping treatment. 21. Known hypersensitivity reactions to peginterferon alfa-2a include urticaria, angioedema, bronchoconstriction, anaphylaxis, and Stevens-Johnson syndrome. 22. Peginterferon alfa-2a is contraindicated in patients with autoimmune hepatitis, hepatic decompensation (Child-Pugh score >6, class B or C) in cirrhotic patients with or without HIV coinfection, and in neonates or infants. 23. Combination therapy with ribavirin is contraindicated in pregnant females and males whose female partners are pregnant. Ribavirin may cause birth defects or fetal death. Refer to the prescribing information of other HCV antiviral drugs, including ribavirin, for additional warnings and precautions.
